trick: Commerce is the wider word: trade is the buying and selling itself, and the auxiliaries are everything that makes trade possible. So commerce equals trade plus aids to trade — banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising.

chapter: Business Services: Banking, Insurance, Transport and Warehousing
trick: Insurance rests on three ideas that get asked again and again: utmost good faith, insurable interest and indemnity. Indemnity means you are restored to your former position, never enriched — which is why you cannot insure a ₹1 lakh car for ₹5 lakh and profit from a crash.

video.query: business services banking insurance principles transport warehousing class 11

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about business services.

items.statement: Under the principle of indemnity, the insured is put back in the position held before the loss.
items.why: Insurance compensates; it does not reward. This is why you cannot profit from a claim.

items.statement: Life insurance is a contract of indemnity.
items.why: Life cannot be valued in money, so a life policy is a contract of assurance for an agreed sum, not indemnity. This is the exception examiners look for.

items.statement: Utmost good faith requires both parties to disclose all material facts.
items.why: Hiding an illness or a fire risk makes the contract voidable, because the insurer priced it on what it was told.

items.statement: A current account normally pays a high rate of interest.
items.why: Current accounts are for frequent business transactions and usually earn no interest. It is fixed deposits that pay the highest rate.
It holds goods from the moment they are produced to the moment they are wanted, which is exactly the creation of time utility.

trick: Keep e-business and outsourcing apart. E-business changes how a firm transacts, by moving it online; outsourcing changes who does the work, by handing it to somebody else. A call centre in Kolkata answering American customers is outsourcing, not e-business.

trick: An entrepreneur is not simply someone who starts a business; the defining act is bearing uncertainty for an innovation. Schumpeter's word for it is creative destruction — the new way of doing things kills the old one, which is why the risk is real.

video.query: entrepreneurship characteristics functions startup India class 11 business studies

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about entrepreneurship.

items.statement: Risk-bearing is an essential function of the entrepreneur.
items.why: Someone must carry the uncertainty of an unknown return, and that is what distinguishes the entrepreneur from a salaried manager.

items.statement: An entrepreneur and a manager are the same thing.
items.why: A manager runs an existing plan for a salary; an entrepreneur conceives the venture and carries the risk of it failing.
Schumpeter defined the entrepreneur precisely as the innovator, whether of a product, a method, a market or a source of supply.

items.statement: Every entrepreneur must be an inventor.
items.why: Inventing creates something new; entrepreneurship brings it to market. Many of the most successful entrepreneurs invented nothing themselves.

items.statement: A start-up needs no plan because ideas matter more than paperwork.
items.why: A business plan is how the idea is tested for feasibility and how finance is raised. Skipping it is one of the commonest causes of failure.
